title: Valence-space associations in vertical touchscreen interactions
author: Sergio Cervera-Torres
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.qagdsbw
materials: Participants were recruited by means of the Online Recruitment System for Economic Experiments (www.orsee.org) Concretely, in this study, participants were able to sign up at most 72 hours before the experimental session took place (e.g., if an experimental session was scheduled on the 04.06 at 12.00 h., the deadline to sign up for the said session was set on the 01.06 at 12.00h) In addition, the candidates were informed that right-hand dominance was set as an inclusion criterion for the experiment. Furthermore, it was specified that, in order to carry out appropriately the experimental task, it was necessary to complete first the valence evaluation of a set of emotional pictures

steps.title: Conduct Pre-Experimental Valence Evaluation
steps.instruction: Administer an online valence evaluation 48 hours before the experimental session using the Questback platform.

substeps.instruction: Provide participants with a link to evaluate 20 positive and 20 negative pictures from the International Affective Picture System (IAPS).
Display pictures centered on the screen in randomized order.
Require participants to rate valence using a 9-point Likert scale (1 = lowest valence, 9 = highest valence).
Ensure participants only observe and rate the pictures without interacting with them.

steps.title: Prepare Participant and Environment
steps.instruction: Set up the participant in a quiet room and collect necessary documentation.

substeps.instruction: Obtain signed informed consent.
Have participants complete the Edinburgh Inventory (Oldfield 1971, modified by Salmaso and Longoni 1985) to determine handedness.

steps.title: Configure Hardware and Ergonomics
steps.instruction: Set up the touchscreen monitor and adjust the participant's seating position.

substeps.instruction: Mount a 23-inch Dell S2340T Activ-Matrix-TFT-LCD touchscreen monitor (resolution 1600 x 900 pixels) vertically on a desk.
Connect the monitor to a computer (Lenovo ThinkPad T410, Intel Core i7 620M, 2.67 GHz).
Ask the participant to extend their right arm toward the center of the screen and adjust the chair height accordingly to ensure consistent reach conditions.

steps.title: Perform Training Trials
steps.instruction: Familiarize the participant with the task using non-emotional stimuli.

substeps.instruction: Conduct four training trials using color squares (red, blue, green, and yellow).
Require participants to touch and swipe the squares across the screen and evaluate their valence.
Ensure the resolution of training stimuli is identical to the emotional pictures (397 x 340 pixels / 10.5 cm x 9 cm).

steps.title: Execute Experimental Valence Rating Task
steps.instruction: Implement the swiping and rating task based on the participant's assigned group.

substeps.instruction: Randomly assign participants to either the downward or upward movement condition.

Downward movement condition: Participants touch and swipe randomly presented pictures with their right hand from the upper border of the monitor toward an empty square (6.2 cm x 6.2 cm) located 42 cm away at the lower border.
Upward movement condition: Participants touch and swipe pictures with their right hand from the lower border toward a white square located at the upper border.
After each swipe, display the picture in the middle of the monitor with a 9-point Likert scale below (1 = lowest valence, 9 = highest valence) for evaluation.
Randomize the presentation order of the IAPS pictures.
Instruct the participant that the researcher will wait outside the room in front of the door during the task to avoid influence on ratings.

steps.title: Complete Session
steps.instruction: Conclude the experiment and provide compensation.

substeps.instruction: Display an end-of-experiment message after the last trial.
Thank and debrief the participant.
Pay the participant 8 euros.
